item.title: Sqwod Daily — Friday, 07 August 2026
item.description: Your marketing budget can't outrun a single bad rep at the door — one Crunch employee just proved it.
item.content:encoded:
Friday, 07 August 2026 View online →
DAILY
The fitness industry, decoded — in five minutes.
Friday, 07 August 2026 · Weekday
Your marketing budget can't outrun a single bad rep at the door — one Crunch employee just proved it.
— Sqwod
Money movement
⇄  Acquired
Thorne
 $3.8bn
P&G acquires supplement brand, signalling big consumer goods moves into fitness nutrition
⇄  Acquired
Jamieson Wellness

Kirin acquires Jamieson to build a North American wellness platform
Connect the dots
One bad front-desk moment beats every retention dollar
A 62-year-old walked into Crunch wanting to use a treadmill and was told to 'get in shape first.' That's not a rogue employee story — it's a systems story. If your front desk has no clear mandate on who you serve and how, every person you hire becomes a brand liability operating on instinct.
The fix isn't a script, it's a standard: who is this gym for, what does every member deserve at the door, and how does staff know when they're getting it wrong? Your retention emails, referral programs, and social ads all assume the member got past hello. When they don't, the math breaks. Audit the first 90 seconds of a member's visit this week like it's your most expensive touchpoint — because it is.
The rundown
01
Judge: Toronto drug cops 'likely' stole $5K from a fitness coach
A Ontario judge stayed a cocaine charge after finding officers probably pocketed $5,000 from a fitness coach during a search — a reminder that if cash goes missing on your premises, the paper trail protecting you matters as much as the money itself.
Source: Toronto Star →
02
$3.8bn bet: P&G just bought supplement brand Thorne
P&G has acquired wellness supplement company Thorne for $3.8 billion, signalling that big consumer goods is done watching fitness nutrition from the sidelines. For studio owners and coaches stocking retail shelves, expect the brand's distribution and marketing firepower to look very different very soon.
Source: Retail Systems →
03
A Crunch Employee Told a 62-Year-Old to 'Get in Shape First'
A woman who just wanted to walk on a treadmill was turned away at the door by a Crunch Fitness employee — a reminder that front-desk culture is your brand, and one bad rep can undo every dollar you've spent on retention.
Source: BroBible →
04
TulaBala Takes Yoga Luxe to Nordstrom.com
The design-forward yoga brand TulaBala just landed on Nordstrom.com — meaning premium wellness gear is now one scroll away from a cashmere sweater. For studio owners and coaches, that's a signal: your clients' expectations around aesthetics and quality are getting a serious upgrade.
Source: WBOC TV →
05
Kirin Is Buying Jamieson Wellness to Crack North America
The Japanese beer-and-health giant is acquiring Jamieson Wellness to build a North American platform — meaning the supplement aisle is about to get a well-funded new landlord worth watching.
Source: NutraIngredients.com →
06
£6,000 raised: PMF Military Fitness Group boots cancer into touch
Droitwich's PMF Military Fitness Group sweated their way to £6,000 for cancer charity — proof that a community fitness group can punch well above its weight when it has a cause worth fighting for.
Source: The Droitwich Standard →
Policy watch
Cash on your premises needs a paper trail — courts agree
An Ontario judge stayed a cocaine charge after finding officers 'likely' stole $5,000 from a fitness coach during a search. If cash changes hands in your studio — from retail sales, sessions, or tips — documented receipts and a cash log aren't just good accounting; they're your only evidence if money goes missing.
Sqwod recs
✓ Track: Start logging your 'door-to-floor' conversion: what percentage of walk-ins or trial enquiries actually become paying members? If you don't know it, you can't improve the first impression that drives it.
✓ Try: Run a 30-day community fundraiser tied to a local cause — set a public goal, post weekly progress, and let your members do the marketing. PMF's model shows cause-led events drive both retention and word-of-mouth better than most paid campaigns.

Connect the dots
Running a studio and running a business aren't the same job
Here's the pattern body LIFE is flagging — and it shows up everywhere: the best coach in the room is often the worst CEO in the building. When your identity is built around training clients, the 'business' tasks (pricing strategy, retention systems, margin review) feel like distractions. They're not. They're the job. The studio is just where the job lives.
The operators who scale aren't necessarily the most technically gifted trainers — they're the ones who clocked the shift early: at some point you stop selling hours and start building a system that sells without you. If your calendar is still full of PT sessions you personally deliver, ask yourself who's minding the business while you're minding the barbell.

item.description: The gym dispute that turned physical in Ahmedabad isn't a crime story — it's a policy design failure with a medical bill attached.
item.content:encoded:

DAILY

Monday, 03 August 2026 · Weekday
The gym dispute that turned physical in Ahmedabad isn't a crime story — it's a policy design failure with a medical bill attached.
— Sqwod
Money movement
▲  Valuation
Kuwait Stock Exchange

Connect the dots
Your cancellation policy is a de-escalation tool
A membership disagreement in Ahmedabad escalated until a businessman got assaulted. That's an extreme outcome, but the friction point is universal: vague or punitive cancellation terms create emotionally charged confrontations at your front desk every single week. The policy isn't just a revenue-protection clause — it's the script your staff reads when someone is already frustrated, already feeling trapped, and already looking for a fight.
So what does a safer policy actually look like? Clear exit windows, no-surprise fees, and a written process your team can point to instead of improvise. When the answer to 'why can't I cancel?' is a laminated sentence on the wall rather than a shrug, the temperature drops fast. Audit your cancellation flow this week — not for churn risk, but for conflict risk. Those are the same conversation, and one of them has a much higher cost.
The rundown
01
Gym membership dispute ends in assault in Ahmedabad
A membership disagreement turned physical in Ahmedabad, leaving a businessman assaulted — a sharp reminder that your cancellation policy isn't just a business decision, it's a safety one.
Source: The Times of India →
02
Garmin's Fitness Revenue Is Surging — and There's More Coming
Garmin's CEO is teasing a 'very rich' product roadmap ahead, which means the wearables arms race your clients are already obsessed with isn't slowing down anytime soon. If you're not factoring device data into your programming conversations, you're going to be playing catch-up.
Source: Athletech News →
03
AI Coaching Just Dealt Itself Into the Poker Game
AceGuardian Technologies has launched QuintAce, an adaptive AI coaching and analytics platform built specifically for poker. If you thought AI-powered performance coaching was only for the gym floor, the table just called your bluff.
Source: ACCESS Newswire →
04
Wearable HAV monitors just got an ISO spotlight
New ISO guidance is pushing wearable hand-arm vibration monitoring into the mainstream — and if your clients work with heavy equipment, this is the kind of data-backed safety layer that turns 'we think it's fine' into 'we can prove it.'
Source: Rail Magazine →
05
KSE books 13.74m dinar profit as Gulf markets find their footing
Kuwait's stock exchange posted a healthy first-half profit of 13.74 million dinars, signaling that regional market confidence is climbing. For studio owners eyeing expansion or investors watching emerging fitness markets, a recovering Gulf economy is worth keeping on your radar.
Source: Times Kuwait →
Policy watch
ISO puts wearable vibration monitoring on the map
New ISO guidance is pushing wearable hand-arm vibration (HAV) monitors toward mainstream adoption — relevant if any of your clients train with or work around heavy equipment. This shifts occupational safety conversations from gut-feel to documented, device-backed data.
Sqwod recs
✓ Steal: Add a one-page 'conflict protocol' to your staff handbook: a scripted, calm response for membership disputes that gives front-desk staff exact phrases to use — removes improvisation and keeps everyone's blood pressure down.
✓ Track: Start logging the reason codes behind every cancellation request — not just the number of cancellations. Patterns in the 'why' are your earliest warning system for programming gaps, pricing friction, and scheduling problems.
✓ Try: Experiment with a 'pause membership' option as a middle layer between active and cancelled — it reduces confrontational cancellations by giving frustrated members a low-stakes off-ramp that often converts back to active within 60 days.

item.description: What if your membership pricing is accidentally optimized for your next investor conversation instead of your next renewal?
item.content:encoded:
Wednesday, 29 July 2026 View online →
DAILY
The fitness industry, decoded — in five minutes.
Wednesday, 29 July 2026 · Weekday
What if your membership pricing is accidentally optimized for your next investor conversation instead of your next renewal?
— Sqwod
Money movement
▲  Raise
Throne Science
 $10M
seed round to build a gut-health monitoring toilet, co-founded by Whoop's former CTO
Connect the dots
When your pricing model serves the deck, not the member
The $19.99 car wash play is a masterclass in recurring-revenue theater: low price = high signup volume = beautiful MRR chart = happy investors. The cars may or may not get clean. Sound familiar? Fitness memberships can fall into exactly the same trap — architect your tiers around churn metrics and cohort retention curves for a future raise, and you quietly stop asking whether the product actually solves the member's problem week to week.
The so-what: audit your membership structure this quarter with one brutal question — 'Would I design this the same way if I never planned to raise money or sell?' If the answer is no, your pricing architecture is sending the wrong signal to your most valuable asset: the people who actually show up. Retention isn't a metric you report; it's a feeling your members have on the way home.
The rundown
01
$19.99/Month Car Washes Are Really Selling Wall Street a Subscription
The Auto Wire flags that cheap car wash memberships are engineered for investor metrics, not clean cars — a useful reminder that any recurring-revenue model can be built around the pitch deck rather than the customer.
Source: The Auto Wire →
02
100 More Gyms: FitActive Is Dead Serious About Italy
The Italian chain just reaffirmed plans to open 100 additional locations, doubling down on ambitions it first laid out at the ATN Summit. If you're watching European fitness expansion, this one's worth a spot on your radar.
Source: Athletech News →
03
$10M to track gut health — from the toilet
Throne Science, co-founded by Whoop's former CTO, just raised $10M to turn your porcelain throne into a health monitor. If your clients are asking about recovery and readiness, gut data from the bathroom might be the next frontier worth watching.
Source: Crunchbase News →
04
Preston fitness firms merge gym, Pilates & recovery for women
A group of Preston fitness businesses has launched a combined women's wellness membership spanning gym access, Pilates, and recovery. For operators eyeing retention, bundled multi-modal memberships are clearly becoming the move worth watching.
Source: Blog Preston →
05
Community gym crowdfunds to beat the heat (and the chill)
Wheathampstead's community gym has launched a Crowdfunder campaign to keep its space comfortable year-round — a reminder that member retention isn't just programming, it's also not sweating through a session in July or freezing in January.
Source: St Albans Times →
06
Mojawa's Purra Flow headphones now coach your clients mid-rep
The new AI-powered bone conduction headphones from Mojawa deliver real-time coaching audio through the skull — not the ears — while workouts happen. For trainers and studio operators, it's a front-row seat to what on-demand, wearable coaching actually looks like at the consumer level.
Source: The Manila Times →
Stat
100
additional gym locations FitActive plans to open in Italy
European fitness expansion is far from saturated — FitActive doubling its footprint signals that mid-market, high-volume club models still have serious runway on the continent.
Sqwod recs
✓ Steal: Run a 'member effort score' survey: one question — 'How easy is it to get value from your membership?' — sent 30 days post-signup. Low scores predict churn weeks before it shows in your data.
✓ Track: Start logging your monthly revenue-per-active-member alongside total MRR — it exposes whether growth is real or just volume masking declining engagement per head.
✓ Try: Map one 'uncomfortable physical moment' in your facility — temperature, noise, parking, lighting — and fix it before adding any new programming. Environment retention is invisible until it isn't.

item.title: Sqwod Daily — Tuesday, 28 July 2026
item.description: The most scalable thing in your studio might not be your square footage — it's the person teaching in it.
item.content:encoded:
Tuesday, 28 July 2026 View online →
DAILY
The fitness industry, decoded — in five minutes.
Tuesday, 28 July 2026 · Weekday
The most scalable thing in your studio might not be your square footage — it's the person teaching in it.
— Sqwod
Money movement
▲  Raise
VEYR
 £1M
UK startup raising to bring AI-powered fitness coaching to market
Connect the dots
Your talent pipeline beats your franchise deck
One LA Pilates studio is quietly doing what most growth-obsessed operators won't: investing in developing instructors instead of opening new doors. It sounds counterintuitive until you realise that franchises export your brand but dilute your culture, while great instructors multiply your culture and carry it into every room they ever teach in. The constraint was never capital — it was people who truly get it.
For studio founders, this reframes the whole expansion question. Before you model out a second location, ask what your instructor development pipeline actually looks like. If your best teachers leave because there's no upward path, you're not scaling — you're churning. The studios that crack retention (member and staff) tend to be the ones that treat instructor growth as a product, not a perk.
The rundown
01
VEYR is raising £1M to bring AI coaching to fitness
The UK startup just launched a £1 million funding round for AI-powered fitness coaching — a signal that investors are betting the next great personal trainer might not need a locker room.
Source: Well Nation →
02
People First: The Secret Behind All-Inclusive Fitness Success
body LIFE breaks down why putting people before programming is the real growth lever in all-inclusive fitness — useful reading if you're wondering why your retention numbers aren't matching your membership numbers.
Source: body LIFE →
03
Float Like a Butterfly, Lift Like a Legend
Luxury fitness brand Pent has launched an equipment collection with the Muhammad Ali Estate, per Business Traveller — and for operators looking to give their floor a serious prestige upgrade, this collab signals that heritage IP is becoming the new premium differentiator in fitness hardware.
Source: Business Traveller →
04
This LA Pilates Studio Is Scaling Instructors, Not Franchises
While competitors chase franchise growth, one LA Pilates studio is betting that developing instructors is the real expansion play. For studio owners, it's a timely reminder that your talent pipeline might be your most scalable asset.
Source: Athletech News →
05
Aging Well Is Big Business — Is Your Marketing Keeping Up?
The Global Wellness Institute is putting a spotlight on the 'Aging Well' category and how brands are (finally) advertising to older adults seriously. If your studio still treats 50+ as an afterthought, you're leaving a very fit, very motivated demographic on the table.
Source: Global Wellness Institute →
06
Oura Ring 4: Great life coach, middling gym buddy
GB News finds the Oura Ring 4 excels at tracking lifestyle habits but falls short as a serious training tool — worth knowing before you recommend it to a client who wants performance data, not just pretty sleep scores.
Source: GB News →
Sqwod recs
✓ Track: Start measuring instructor tenure alongside member retention — if your staff churn rate is high, your member churn will follow within 90 days. Run the numbers monthly.
✓ Steal: Create a simple '50+ onboarding script' for your front desk: different language, different goals, different wins than a 30-year-old. Older adults respond to capability framing ('what you'll be able to do') over aesthetics — update your intake form to reflect that.
✓ Try: Run a 30-minute 'teach-back' session monthly where junior instructors coach a segment in front of peers — it accelerates development faster than shadowing alone and costs nothing but calendar time.

$60M AI Coaching Deal Comes to the Sydney Marathon
The Sydney Marathon is rolling out an AI coaching program valued at over $60 million — proof that the race to own runner training just got a whole lot more expensive to enter.

02
Garmin just bought TrainingPeaks — and Connect+ isn't going anywhere
Garmin's acquisition of TrainingPeaks, paired with its Cirqa coaching platform, signals the company is doubling down on its premium Connect+ tier rather than walking it back. For coaches and operators already in the Garmin ecosystem, the writing's on the wall: start factoring subscription costs into your client onboarding conversations.
Source: TechRadar →
03
$1.2M Pilot Pays Off: Luxphy Bets on Your Revenue to Earn Its Own
Luxphy just launched a performance-based profit recovery service for mid-market ecommerce brands — meaning they only win when you do. If you run any kind of online merch, programming, or supplement side to your fitness business, this is the model worth watching.
Source: The Manila Times →
04
Gym Launch drops an industry-first Member Acquisition Dashboard
Gym Launch has unveiled what it's calling the industry's first Member Acquisition Dashboard — and for studio owners tired of guessing where their new members actually come from, this could be the clarity upgrade your growth strategy's been missing.

Ōura's Doug Sweeny on Making Wellness Actually Useful
Yahoo Tech caught up with Ōura's Doug Sweeny at Cannes for Marketing Vanguard, where he made the case for why the smart ring is turning wellness data into something you can actually use.
